key_insight: A variational thermo-mechanical phase transformation model couples heat flow, finite-strain mechanics, and first- and second-order glass transitions to predict vitrification and residual stress during glass additive manufacturing.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers forecast warpage, stress buildup, and microstructure locking under extreme thermal histories in laser-based glass printing.
method: Extended Hamilton principle for coupled thermal, mechanical, and phase-transformation fields
Finite-strain kinematic split with thermal expansion, density change, and viscoelastic deformation
Temperature-dependent viscosity and monolithic Neighbored Element Method for stable heat-equation solution
evidence_signal: The abstract reports material-point validation against TTT behavior across cooling rates and 3D ANSYS deposition simulations showing residual stress accumulation and macroscopic warpage.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on calibrated thermodynamic and viscosity laws, and the monolithic NEM/ANSYS workflow may require careful implementation for strongly coupled, highly transient cooling processes.
paper_title: First- and Second-Order Phase Transformation Modeling Based on the Hamilton Principle: A Coupled Thermo-Mechanical Approach for Glass Additive Manufacturing
